**UNO – Quick‑Start Rules** | Section | What you need | |---------|---------------| | **Deck** | Standard UNO set (108 cards):
• 90 numbered cards (0–9) in four colors (Red, Green, Blue, Yellow).
• 8 “Skip” cards, 8 “Reverse”, 8 “Draw Two”.
• 4 “Wild” and 4 “Wild Draw Four.” | | **Goal** | Be the first player to score at least 500 points across multiple rounds. Points come from opponents’ remaining cards when someone goes out. | --- ### 1️⃣ Setup 1. Shuffle the full deck thoroughly. 2. Deal each player **7 cards** face down. * If playing with more than 10 players, deal fewer cards or use two decks. 3. Place the rest of the deck facedown as the draw pile. 4. Flip the top card of the draw pile onto its side; this becomes the discard pile’s starting card. *If the flipped card is an action card (`+2`, `Skip`, etc.), treat it like any other card—no penalty applies until your turn.* 5. Determine who plays first (e.g., highest card value, youngest player). --- ### 2️⃣ Turn Order & Flow Players take turns clockwise unless a Reverse changes direction. On your turn: 1. **Play one card** from hand if possible: - Must match either color OR numeric/letter value of the top discard. - Wilds can always be played regardless of color/value. 2. After discarding, **draw a new card** from the draw pile so you end up back with 7 cards again (unless you went out). 3. If you cannot play anything, simply draw one card. You may then immediately play that drawn card if legal. --- ### 3️⃣ Action Cards | Card | Effect on next player(s) | Notes | |------|--------------------------|-------| | **Skip** | Next player loses their turn. | | | **Reverse** | Changes play order direction. In a 2‑player game, acts like Skip. | | | **Draw Two (+2)** | Next player draws two cards AND misses their turn. | | | **Wild** | Player chooses the active color after playing. | | | **Wild Draw Four (+4)** | Same as Wild but forces next player to draw four cards. | Can only be used if you have no playable card matching the current color. If challenged correctly, the challenger must instead draw six cards. | #### Challenging +4 When another player uses a Wild Draw Four, anyone whose turn comes next may challenge: - **Challenge accepted?** • If the challenging player actually had a valid card of the previous color, they lose the round and must pick up all seven cards currently in the discard pile plus the original +4 card. • If not, the challenger draws six cards (instead of just four), and the +4 remains in effect. - **No challenge:** Play continues normally. --- ### 4️⃣ Going Out (“UNO!”) - When you’re left with **one card**, shout “UNO!” before your opponent takes their turn. Failure to do so results in drawing two extra cards as a penalty. - On your last turn, if you play your second-to-last card leaving zero cards, you win the round instantly. --- ### 5️⃣ Scoring After a round ends: 1. Each opponent tallies the point values of the cards still in their hands: * Numbered cards → Face value (0–9). * Skip / Reverse / Draw Two → 20 pts each. * Wild / Wild Draw Four → 50 pts each. 2. Add those totals together; that sum is added to the winner’s overall score. 3. Continue playing additional rounds until somebody reaches **≥ 500 points** (or whatever target you agree upon). --- ### 6️⃣ Variations & House Rules | Variation | How It Works | |-----------|--------------| | **“Stacking”** | Players may stack +2/+4 cards on top of each other, forcing the total to accumulate. Some groups allow stacking while others don’t. | | **“Seven-O”** | Playing a 7 lets you swap hands with any player; playing an 0 reverses play direction and everyone passes their entire hand to the person opposite them. | | **“Jump-In”** | If you see exactly the same card as the top discard during another player's turn, you may jump ahead and play it immediately. | | **“Custom Decks”** | Use themed sets (Mario, Pokémon, etc.) – scoring stays the same. | Feel free to tweak or add house rules! The core mechanics above keep gameplay fast, fun, and competitive. Enjoy your UNO sessions!
